This is a known configuration issue, not a Vite bug. The excluded ESM package dynamically imports `react-tiny-popover`, whose published entry is CommonJS; because that nested dependency is not discovered during the initial crawl, it is served unbundled and fails at runtime [3]. The fix is to explicitly include that nested CommonJS dependency:

```js
optimizeDeps: {
  include: ['internal-ui > react-tiny-popover']
}
```

This resolves the reproduction, and Vite's docs already call out including nested CommonJS dependencies of excluded ESM packages [2][3]. A Vite member confirmed this is correct and that no Vite code change is needed unless the report still reproduces with that nested dependency included [2].

answer: This is a known limitation, not intended behavior. `optimizeDeps` is documented to work on deps only, and the Vite team has no plans to make it work for normal files [4]. The cause is structural: in `vite:resolve` and `vite:pre-alias`, `tryOptimizedResolve` sits behind `if (bareImportRE.test(id))` and matches optimizer metadata by specifier string rather than resolved file path, so a relative import resolving to the included file never hits the pre-bundle [3]. A fix was proposed in #23432 that matches relative imports against optimized metadata using the final resolved source path while preserving `?raw`, worker, and URL query handling [1]. However, a maintainer said passing source files doesn't cause issues and isn't documented to work, so fixing/tracking isn't necessary—though a simple guard PR would be considered [4]. The experimental `bundledDev` feature is meant to address the many-project-files problem [4].
judge_reason: Candidate matches the reference's resolution (deps-only limitation, no plans to fix, bundledDev as the intended solution, guard PR acceptable) and adds consistent technical detail without contradicting it.

Under `experimental.bundledDev`, `hotUpdate` is invoked with `this.environment` undefined because `ROLLUP_HOOKS` in `packages/vite/src/node/constants.ts` includes `watchChange` but not `hotUpdate`, so `injectEnvironmentToHooks` in `packages/vite/src/node/build.ts` never creates an environment-bound wrapper for it and the hook runs with the engine's bare plugin context [4]. Plugins following the documented `hotUpdate` pattern then throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` on every edit, and the error is captured as a build error so the dev server serves stale output until restart [5].

A narrow fix was opened in #23317, scoped to wrapping `hotUpdate` inside `injectEnvironmentToHooks` (not the broader adapter work in #22956), with a unit test asserting `this.environment.name` is set [2]. Separately, sapphi-red notes this was "kind of fixed" by rolldown/rolldown#10837 in Rolldown v1.2.8, since `hotUpdate` is now not called temporarily [1]. However, a later commenter reports the issue is still present and the opened PRs have been closed [3].

This is a bug in the object-rest lowering used when building with `target: ["safari11"]` in Vite 8, where nested destructuring with object rest/spread is transformed into invalid output containing `{} = null`, causing `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot destructure 'null' as it is null.` [4]. Until that fix reaches Rolldown and Vite, you can work around it by splitting the destructuring into separate declarations [5]:

```js
const { ariaAttributes: s, style: r, ...n } = e
const { ariaAttributes: i, style: l, ...f } = t
```

Changing only `build.minify` does not avoid it, but a target that doesn't need object-rest lowering (e.g. `safari12`) does, if acceptable [5].

The bug is that the injected modern-browser detection script sets `window.__vite_is_modern_browser=true` even on browsers that don't support `import.meta.resolve`, so the legacy-loading fallback (`if(window.__vite_is_modern_browser)return`) always returns early and legacy chunks never load [1][5]. The injected snippet is:

```html
<script type="module">import'data:text/javascript,if(!import.meta.resolve)throw Error("import.meta.resolve not supported")';import.meta.url;import("_").catch(()=>1);(async function*(){})().next();window.__vite_is_modern_browser=true</script>
```

Because the `import.meta.resolve` check is thrown inside a `data:text/javascript` import rather than the main thread, it doesn't stop execution, so `__vite_is_modern_browser=true` is still set [5]. Moving the `import.meta.resolve` check into the main thread reportedly allows legacy chunks to load on Safari <16 [1][4]. The issue is labeled `plugin: legacy` and `p4-important` [1].

answer: Dynamic imports in UMD builds aren't supported by Rollup. To make them work, Vite enables `output.inlineDynamicImports`, but that does not preserve execution order [1]. As a result, the logs appear as `[1] => [2] => [4] => [3]` instead of the expected `[1] => [2] => [3] => [4]`, while dev mode and ES-format production builds are correct [3]. This is tracked as an upstream Rollup issue [1]. Per a maintainer, the execution order is preserved in Vite 8+ and Rolldown [4].
judge_reason: The candidate agrees with the reference that execution order is preserved in Vite 8+ and Rolldown, adding consistent context about the UMD/Rollup limitation.

answer: Setting `server.hmr: false` disables HMR, but it does not disable the WebSocket connection: WebSocket is used for features other than HMR, so it cannot be disabled [1]. That's why you still see "failed to connect to WebSocket" errors even with HMR off [2]. There is no supported way to turn the WebSocket off; the only workaround mentioned is a temporary Chrome DevTools override that makes `setupWebSocket` return `null` [3]. One reported reason to want this is that a WebSocket prevents pages from entering the back/forward cache [4].
judge_reason: Candidate agrees with the reference that server.hmr:false disables HMR but WebSocket cannot be disabled, adding consistent context without conflicting versions or issues.
